content: Updated swag/docker-compose.yaml — removed deprecated 'version: 2.1' field; replaced hardcoded placeholder values (URL, EMAIL, EXTRA_DOMAINS) with env-var references (SWAG_URL, SWAG_EMAIL, etc.) documented with inline comments; added mcp-net (external, name: \${MCP_NETWORK:-mcp-oauth}) and jakenet (external) network entries so SWAG can reach auth:8000 and other MCP services; added second volume mount binding \${SWAG_PROXY_CONFS_PATH:-./proxy-confs} to /config/nginx/proxy-confs for nginx proxy-conf files; moved port values to quoted strings per compose best practices.

Three traefik references existed in justfile: (1) line 210: 'docker volume create traefik-certificates || true' in volumes-create recipe - removed entirely; (2) line 672: 'docker exec traefik cat /certificates/acme.json 2>/dev/null | jq -r ...' cert inspection command in check-certs/health recipe - replaced with 'docker exec swag cat /config/etc/letsencrypt/live/\${BASE_DOMAIN}/cert.pem 2>/dev/null'; (3) line 220: comment '# Generate Traefik middlewares from template with environment variables' above generate-middlewares recipe - updated to reference SWAG instead

Renamed log_traefik_headers() to log_proxy_headers() for proxy-agnostic naming. Made x-forwarded-server default to empty string '' instead of None so it survives the None-filter and is logged as an empty string (not omitted) when absent — avoids misleading absence vs. unknown distinction. Updated all traefik_headers variable references to proxy_headers, updated comments to be proxy-agnostic (mentions Traefik, SWAG/nginx, Caddy), and changed the CORS comment from 'not behind Traefik' to 'not behind a proxy that handles CORS'.

nginx auth_request does NOT automatically forward upstream response headers to the backend like Traefik ForwardAuth did — requires explicit auth_request_set + proxy_set_header for X-User-Id, X-User-Name, X-Auth-Token

nginx processes if-blocks in the rewrite phase BEFORE auth_request runs — so OPTIONS requests with a return inside the if block bypass auth_request entirely. This is correct CORS behavior (browsers need unauthenticated preflights) but must be documented as intentional

/.well-known/oauth-client-id-metadata MUST have an explicit nginx location block without auth_request — the catch-all location / has auth_request which would return 401 to unauthenticated clients bootstrapping the MCP 2025-11-25 OAuth flow

PATTERN: Every auth_request-protected nginx location block needs 4 extra lines: auth_request_set for each identity header + proxy_set_header to forward them downstream. Forgetting these creates silent per-user identity loss

Bare except: in Python catches SystemExit and KeyboardInterrupt — always use specific exception types (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError) for parse error handling. Ctrl+C appears broken to users when swallowed by bare except in a wait loop

Auth codes in this system expire in 10 minutes (changed in commit 79b8c84 for MCP 2025-11-25 spec) — NOT 1 year. Several comments in test files had stale 1-year TTL documentation

content: config.py migrated to OAUTH_* prefixed pydantic aliases simultaneously with auth/docker-compose.yml dropping explicit environment: mappings — without updating .env.example, fresh deployments get ValidationError on startup. Root cause: two coordinated changes with no single file showing both sides of the contract.

nginx include directives are resolved at parse time (text paste), NOT at request time — placing an include inside an if block does NOT prevent the outer include from also executing. Both copies of _cors_headers.conf are always sent, producing duplicate CORS headers that browsers reject.

sys.exit() inside pytest hooks — calling sys.exit() in pytest_configure or session-scoped fixtures raises SystemExit, bypassing pytest teardown. Always use pytest.exit('reason', returncode=1) which triggers proper fixture finalization and avoids orphaned containers.

fetch_client_metadata() validates HTTPS scheme but not resolved IP ranges — DNS rebinding can bypass HTTPS-only check by registering a DNS name that initially resolves to a public IP (passing validation) then rebinding to an internal IP after TTL expiry. SSRF fix must check post-resolution IP, not just URL scheme.

nginx auth_request does NOT automatically forward upstream response headers to the proxied backend. Headers from /verify must be explicitly captured with auth_request_set and then forwarded with proxy_set_header. Without this, MCP services receive no user identity information despite auth succeeding.

bare except: in service readiness checks — catches KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit in addition to expected exceptions, making Ctrl+C unresponsive during health polling. Always specify exception types: except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError) as e:

mcp-template.subdomain.conf location blocks for /.well-known/ only route to the auth service, not to individual MCP services. The oauth-client-id-metadata endpoint must be served by the auth service (mcp-oauth:8000) with Cache-Control headers and NO auth_request, since unauthenticated clients fetch it during OAuth bootstrapping.

docs/_toc.yml is a Jupyter Book table of contents file — deleting docs/services/traefik.md without updating _toc.yml causes the documentation build to fail with a missing file error. Always update _toc.yml when adding/removing docs pages.

/health endpoint behavior changed from 401 (Traefik-era, required auth) to 200 (SWAG-era, public health check for nginx upstream monitoring). Test assertions that checked for 401 on /health are now wrong — test must be updated to expect 200.

PATTERN: unguarded int() conversion on env var string — MCP_UPSTREAM_PORT from environment is a string; int() raises ValueError on non-numeric input (empty string, 'tcp://...', etc.). Always use try/except ValueError or validate before converting. This crashes the config generator for every new MCP service setup.

/introspect route was missing from mcp-template.subdomain.conf — RFC 7662 clients that call /introspect through the MCP subdomain (not auth subdomain) would get 404. Introspect should be proxied to auth service WITHOUT auth_request (like /token and /register).

PATTERN: nginx .conf generation with unsanitized env vars — scripts/generate_ai_routes.py writes hostname/service values from environment directly into nginx conf files. A value containing ';' or '{' breaks nginx config syntax and could be exploited for conf injection. Validate hostname format (alphanumeric, hyphens, dots only) before writing.

NEO4J_PASSWORD was hardcoded in git history (servers/mcp-neo4j-memory/ files that were deleted but remain in git objects). Rotating the password via git history rewrite or gh secret scanning is needed. Future: never commit passwords even in deleted service subdirectories.

mcp-template.docker-compose.yml healthcheck was replaced from the MCP protocol-level initialize handshake to a simple wget HTTP check during the SWAG migration. The MCP initialize handshake is required by spec to verify the service is actually speaking MCP, not just accepting TCP connections. A service can pass a wget health check while being broken at the MCP protocol layer.

routes.py /error endpoint interpolates raw query params (error, error_description) into an f-string HTML template without html.escape() — reflected XSS on the auth domain. The /callback handler redirects to /error with user-influenced error_description values, making this exploitable via crafted OAuth state injection." && \
refresh_token grant loads refresh_data from Redis but never validates refresh_data['client_id'] == current client_id. A stolen refresh token is redeemable by any registered client. OAuth 2.1 and RFC 6749 §10.4 require refresh tokens to be bound to the issuing client." && \
public client refresh token rotation copies username/scope/client_id into the new token but omits the 'resources' RFC 8707 field from refresh_data. The second refresh cycle issues an access token with no audience, which AsyncResourceProtector rejects as invalid_audience. Silent fail — the first refresh succeeds, the second doesn't." && \
.env.example sets REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379 but auth/docker-compose.yml service is named 'mcp-oauth-redis'. The auth service starts successfully (REDIS_URL is just a string) but every request fails at Redis connection time. Appears healthy via process check but broken at runtime.

Dockerfile COPY src/ appears before RUN uv pip install — correct order is copy only pyproject.toml → install deps → copy src/. Any src/ change invalidates the install layer cache causing 30-90s full dependency reinstall. Classic Docker layer ordering mistake." && \
PATTERN: pytest-xdist module-level mutable globals — under xdist, each worker gets its own copy of the module. A session-level cleanup fixture in the main process never sees workers' appended values. _TEST_CLIENT_REGISTRY is empty in the main process at cleanup time. Always document xdist behavior for shared state; prefer per-fixture cleanup over session-level fallbacks.
